activity.notes: Reviewed seed Activity used only to create the distinct medieval Kingdom of Italy identity associated with the Holy Roman imperial polity complex. Otto I acquired the Italian kingship in 951 and retained it until his death in 973. The parenthetical English and Korean labels are ATLAS disambiguators used to distinguish this medieval regnum Italicum from the separate Napoleonic kingdom of 1805–1814 and the modern Kingdom of Italy of 1861–1946.

sources.title: Il regno italico — Treccani
sources.citation_text: Treccani describes the medieval regnum Italicum and explains that under Otto I the kingdom was incorporated into the Holy Roman imperial context.

sources.title: Italia — Dizionario di Storia, Treccani
sources.citation_text: Treccani states that Otto entered Italy in 951–952, was proclaimed King of Italy at Pavia, and in 962 united the Italian crown with the Holy Roman imperial crown.
